unexecuted edits in the UI.</span></div></section><section class="step" id="step-3"><div class="step-head"><span class="step-no">03</span><h2>Filtering & sample QC</h2></div><p class="step-intro">Separate sample exclusion, low-expression filtering and variable-gene selection. These are distinct decisions.</p><div class="story"><p>The example starts with <strong>18 samples × 24,000 genes</strong>. The user manually excluded <strong>Mut_Drought_r3</strong>, leaving 17 samples. Raw read counts are used without transformation.</p></div><div class="story"><p>A gene is removed for low expression if its read count is below 10 in <strong>more than 50% of retained samples</strong>. With 17 samples, this means <strong>at least 9 samples</strong> below 10. This step removes 7,600 genes and leaves 16,400.</p></div><div class="story"><p>Next, 400 genes with no variation across samples are removed. The remaining genes are ranked by <strong>median absolute deviation (MAD)</strong>, which describes how much expression varies between samples. The top <strong>8,000 genes</strong> enter network analysis; another 8,000 are not selected. Genes outside the top set may still be biologically meaningful.</p></div><div class="flow"><div><small>Input</small><b>24,000</b><small>18 samples</small></div><span>→</span><div><small>After low-expression filter</small><b>16,400</b><small>17 samples</small></div><span>→</span><div><small>After constant-gene filter</small><b>16,000</b><small>MAD > 0</small></div><span>→</span><div><small>Network input</small><b>8,000</b><small>Top 8,000 by MAD</small></div></div><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Excluded sample</th><th>Action</th><th>Reason</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="removed"><td>Mut_Drought_r3</td><td>Manually excluded</td><td>Not provided; no inferred quality issue</td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class="download-row"><a class="button primary" href="../result/02_filter/expression_filtered.preview.tsv" download>Download matrix sample · 8 rows</a><a href="../result/02_filter/removed_samples.tsv" download>Download exclusion log</a></div><p class="caption">Production export: result/02_filter/expression_filtered.tsv, containing the complete 8,000-gene × 17-sample matrix. The 8-row preview demonstrates the link only.</p><figure><img src="../result/02_filter/sample-tree.svg" alt="Sample dendrogram before exclusion; annotation rows: condition, genotype."><figcaption><span><b>Figure 1.</b> Sample dendrogram before exclusion; annotation rows: condition, genotype.</span><a href="../result/02_filter/sample-tree.svg" download>Download SVG ↗</a></figcaption><div class="reading">How to read: nearby branches indicate more similar expression profiles. Annotation rows follow the selected order: condition, genotype, using the app default category palette. The red label marks a manual exclusion. This layout illustration cannot identify actual outliers. Production reports retain both before-exclusion and final trees, reusing the app leaf order, annotation rows, labels and colors.</div></figure></section><section class="step" id="step-4"><div class="step-head"><span class="step-no">04</span><h2>Soft threshold</h2></div><p class="step-intro">Inspect candidate values, then record the chosen power and the reason for choosing it.</p><div class="story"><p>This example uses a signed network with <strong>β = 8</strong>, the first illustrative candidate to reach R² ≥ 0.85. Power strengthens the contrast between stronger and weaker correlations. The production report also includes mean connectivity and scale-free diagnostic plots, and states whether power was recommended or manually chosen.</p></div><figure><img src="../result/03_soft_threshold/soft-threshold.svg" alt="Candidate powers and fit index (synthetic curve)."><figcaption><span><b>Figure 2.</b> Candidate powers and fit index (synthetic curve).</span><a href="../result/03_soft_threshold/soft-threshold.svg" download>Download SVG ↗</a></figcaption><div class="reading">How to read: candidate power is on the x-axis, fit index on the y-axis. The dashed line is the target; the brown point is the chosen power. Reaching the target alone does not establish network reliability.</div></figure></section><section class="step" id="step-5"><div class="step-head"><span class="step-no">05</span><h2>Network & modules</h2></div><p class="step-intro">Group genes with similar expression patterns and record unassigned genes.</p><div class="story"><p>Genes are clustered using topological overlap in a signed network. Minimum module size is 30; the module-merging distance threshold is 0.25. The example contains <strong>4 modules</strong> and <strong>200 unassigned grey genes</strong>; grey is excluded from the module count.</p></div><figure><img src="../result/04_network/modules.svg" alt="Gene clustering and module assignments (illustration)."><figcaption><span><b>Figure 3.</b> Gene clustering and module assignments (illustration).</span><a href="../result/04_network/modules.svg" download>Download SVG ↗</a></figcaption><div class="reading">How to read: genes with the same assignment color belong to one module. Colors act as module names. Production export preserves the app pre/post-merge rows and their labels.</div></figure><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Module</th><th>Gene count</th><th>Share of network input</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr ><td><span style="color:#368f9b">●</span> turquoise</td><td>2,700</td><td>33.75%</td></tr><tr ><td><span style="color:#5373ae">●</span> blue</td><td>2,200</td><td>27.50%</td></tr><tr ><td><span style="color:#ae7865">●</span> brown</td><td>1,800</td><td>22.50%</td></tr><tr ><td><span style="color:#8b9366">●</span> green</td><td>1,100</td><td>13.75%</td></tr><tr ><td><span style="color:#a1a6a3">●</span> grey</td><td>200</td><td>2.50%</td></tr></tbody></table></div></section><section class="step" id="step-6"><div class="step-head"><span class="step-no">06</span><h2>Module–trait</h2></div><p class="step-intro">Summarize module expression using its eigengene, then compare it with selected traits.</p><div class="story"><p>A module eigengene (ME) summarizes the main pattern of module expression; it is not a single representative gene. The heatmap shows ME–trait correlation. Actual results must also display p-values, the statistical test and whether multiple comparisons were adjusted.</p></div><figure><img src="../result/05_module_trait/module-trait.svg" alt="Module–trait heatmap; illustrative layout and color scale."><figcaption><span><b>Figure 4.</b> Module–trait heatmap; illustrative layout and color scale.</span><a href="../result/05_module_trait/module-trait.svg" download>Download SVG ↗</a></figcaption><div class="reading">How to read: red indicates positive correlation and blue negative correlation; deeper colors indicate larger absolute correlations. Correlation does not imply causation. This illustration has no actual p-values and makes no significance claims.</div></figure></section><section class="step" id="step-7"><div class="step-head"><span class="step-no">07</span><h2>Detail & enrichment</h2></div><p class="step-intro">Inspect gene-level patterns and functional context for the selected module and trait.</p><div class="download-row"><span class="pill">Selected module: turquoise</span><span class="pill">Selected trait: Drought</span></div><figure><img src="../result/06_module_detail/turquoise/gs-mm.svg" alt="GS versus module membership (synthetic points)."><figcaption><span><b>Figure 5.</b> GS versus module membership (synthetic points).</span><a href="../result/06_module_detail/turquoise/gs-mm.svg" download>Download SVG ↗</a></figcaption><div class="reading">How to read: each point is a gene. Larger |kME| indicates stronger alignment with the module; larger |GS| indicates stronger association with the trait. Dashed lines illustrate selection boundaries. Actual figures follow the app correlation direction, thresholds and axes.</div></figure><figure><img src="../result/06_module_detail/turquoise/enrichment.svg" alt="GO enrichment dot plot (synthetic terms and values)."><figcaption><span><b>Figure 6.</b> GO enrichment dot plot (synthetic terms and values).</span><a href="../result/06_module_detail/turquoise/enrichment.svg" download>Download SVG ↗</a></figcaption><div class="reading">How to read: each row is a functional term; horizontal position indicates the selected-gene ratio. Actual dot size, color scale, adjusted p-values and GO/KEGG backgrounds follow app settings. This illustration makes no enrichment claims. Missing backgrounds, unrun analyses and no significant terms must be reported as distinct states.</div></figure></section><section class="step" id="step-8"><div class="step-head"><span class="step-no">08</span><h2>Hub genes</h2></div><p class="step-intro">Distinguish candidate selection from the displayed network size.</p><div class="story"><p>For turquoise and Drought, this example selects candidates using <strong>|kME| ≥ 0.8 and |GS| ≥ 0.5</strong>, yielding 42 illustrative candidates. The network displays at most 30 hubs, up to 20 neighbors per hub and edges with weight at least 0.02. Production reports must reflect the engine comparison operators, ranking and limits, and export all candidates as well as displayed nodes and edges.</p></div><figure><img src="../result/07_hub/turquoise/Drought/network.svg" alt="Network layout illustration; not actual module connections."><figcaption><span><b>Figure 7.</b> Network layout illustration; not actual module connections.</span><a href="../result/07_hub/turquoise/Drought/network.svg" download>Download SVG ↗</a></figcaption><div class="reading">How to read: nodes represent genes; edges represent co-expression links passing the threshold. This figure demonstrates visual style only. Production export uses the current app nodes, edges, positions, labels, sizes and colors to prevent random rearrangement.</div></figure></section><section class="step" id="step-9"><div class="step-head"><span class="step-no">09</span><h2>Files & reproducibility</h2></div><p class="step-intro">Keep figures, data and analysis settings within reach.</p><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Contents</th><th>Path</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr ><td>HTML</td><td>report/index.html</td><td>Report entry in the chosen language</td></tr><tr ><td>Quarto</td><td>report/report.qmd</td><td>Editable, re-renderable report source</td></tr><tr ><td>Figures & tables</td><td>result/01_input/ … 07_hub/</td><td>Organized by report step</td></tr><tr ><td>Reading guide</td><td>result/README.txt</td><td>File index, columns and interpretation</td></tr><tr ><td>Analysis provenance</td><td>result/00_provenance/</td><td>Final parameters, view state, environment and checksums</td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class="download-row"><a class="button" href="../result/README.txt" download>Download reading guide</a><a href="../result/00_provenance/view-state.json" download>Example view snapshot</a><a href="report.qmd" download>Download Quarto source</a></div><div class="reading">This preview uses local SVG, CSS and JavaScript, with no external fonts or chart CDN. Copy the complete project folder to open report/index.html offline.
